content.content:
Continuous Monitoring of Postpartum Blood Pressure

The COMPASS study evaluates continuous blood pressure monitoring with wearable technology to improve cardiovascular outcomes for women after pregnancy.

block1.title: About COMPASS
block1.content:
The **COMPASS** study (Continuous Monitoring of Postpartum Blood Pressure for Assessment and Shifting of Cardiovascular Risk) is a clinical trial within the **EXIT-CVD** research consortium, co-funded by the **European Union Innovative Health Initiative (IHI)**.
Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy affect approximately 10% of pregnancies and significantly increase long-term cardiovascular risk. COMPASS evaluates whether continuous blood pressure monitoring via validated wearable technology can improve postpartum BP control and cardiovascular outcomes.

block2.title: Study at a Glance
block2.content:
| | |
|---|---|
| **100** Participants | **3** Clinical Sites |
| **6 months** Participation | **Randomised** Controlled Trial |

Led by **King's College London**, with sites at King's College Hospital, St Thomas' Hospital, and UMC Utrecht.

blocks.title: Powered by Onsentia & RADAR-base
blocks.content:
Onsentia powers the digital data collection and remote monitoring infrastructure for the COMPASS study using the open-source **RADAR-base** platform.
The platform combines: - **Active monitoring (aRMT)** — Patient-reported outcome questionnaires - **Passive monitoring (pRMT)** — Sensor and wearable data collection - **Huawei D2 Watch** — Continuous blood pressure monitoring Integrated with **Megi-Mum** for AI-powered cardiovascular and maternal heart care assessments, and **CogStack** for identifying eligible participants from medical records.

content.title: Study Objectives
content.content:
**Primary:** Evaluate if continuous BP monitoring with wearable devices and clinician-supervised antihypertensive titration improves diastolic BP control at 6 months postpartum compared to standard care.

**Secondary:** Assess acceptability and adherence, determine clinical outcomes, evaluate patient-reported experiences, assess cost-effectiveness, and develop personalised risk prediction models.

content.title: Part of EXIT-CVD
content.content: COMPASS is one of the "early exit" studies within the **EXIT-CVD** consortium, which brings together 42 partners across 17 countries to transform how cardiovascular disease is detected, monitored and treated across Europe.

blocks.title: Why This Matters
blocks.content:
Postpartum hypertension remains inadequately monitored despite contributing substantially to maternal morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence indicates that postpartum BP control critically influences long-term cardiovascular health.
COMPASS uses validated wearable technology to offer real-time, precise BP tracking — potentially enabling improved therapeutic interventions, better patient engagement, and improved cardiovascular outcomes for women after pregnancy.

items.title: 1. Check eligibility and provide consent
items.content: Complete a brief eligibility check, read the Participant Information Sheet, and sign an electronic consent form.

items.title: 2. Set up your study account
items.content: Create an account with your email and a password. Verify your email to proceed.

items.title: 3. Connect your devices
items.content: Connect the Huawei D2 Watch, install the RADAR Active App (aRMT) for questionnaires, and the RADAR Passive App (pRMT) for passive data collection.

items.title: 4. Participate in monitoring
items.content: Wear the Huawei D2 Watch as instructed for continuous blood pressure monitoring, complete questionnaires via the Active App, and keep the Passive App running on your smartphone. The study lasts approximately 6 months.
